title: (Senior) DevOps Engineer - Infrastructure & Security (m/f/d)
description:
Du willst Infrastruktur nicht nur betreiben, sondern verantworten? Bei uns gehört dir der komplette Stack - vom Proxmox-Cluster im eigenen Rechenzentrum über Firewalls und VPNs bis zu AWS und den Deployment-Pipelines.
Testsieger ist eines der größten Vergleichsportale Deutschlands: 4,2 Millionen Produkte, Testberichte, Kundenbewertungen und ein integrierter Preisvergleich, der Millionen Nutzer zum richtigen Kauf führt. Ein 20-köpfiges Team mit direkten Wegen und ohne Konzern-Overhead.
Du übernimmst die Rolle des technischen Owners für unsere Infrastruktur - mit einem Team an deiner Seite, und einem Engineering-Team, das auf dich zählt.
Aufgaben

Du verantwortest den Betrieb unserer Linux-Serverlandschaft: On-Premise-Cluster (Proxmox, ZFS) und AWS
Du betreibst und härtest Netzwerk und Security: Firewalls, VPN, Zugriffskontrolle, Zertifikate, Hardening - inklusive der Netzanbindung an unseren größten Partner
Du automatisierst mit Ansible und hältst Infrastruktur versioniert, reproduzierbar und dokumentiert
Du betreust unsere Container-Plattform (Docker, Nomad, Traefik) und die CI/CD-Pipelines (GitHub Actions), damit die Teams sicher und schnell shippen
Du administrierst MySQL in Produktion: Backups, Performance, Recovery
Du baust Monitoring, Logging und Alerting aus (Grafana, New Relic) und führst Incidents zur Ursache
Du bist Sparringspartner für Engineering, Data und Product - und erklärst, warum Dinge so gebaut sind, wie sie gebaut sind

Qualifikation

Mehrjährige Erfahrung im Betrieb von Linux-Serverumgebungen (Debian/Ubuntu) - du weißt, wie man Systeme auch ohne Assistenz von A nach B bringt
Fundierte Netzwerkkenntnisse: TCP/IP, Routing, DNS, Load Balancing, Firewall- und VPN-Administration
Nachweisbare Praxis in Infrastructure Security: Hardening, Access Control, Security Best Practices
Ansible in Produktion, Container

title: Data Consultant

• Professional conduct at all working levels within a client organization and Parexel .

Experience and Skills

• Demonstrated relevant experience in health economics modeling and model adaptations for at least 3 years - this is a must.

• Able to work across several products/indications in oncology, vaccines, and other global pharma products.

• Experienced and knowledgeable in model adaptation to review Markov, partition-survival models, discrete-event simulation, etc.

• A high degree of written accuracy and attention to detail

• Good communication skills, both oral and in writing, especially in the relaying of technical information

• Self-motivation, enthusiasm, ambition, and flexibility

Education

• Minimum Master's degree, in Health Economics, Biostatistics, Health Services Research, Decision Sciences, Actuarial Sciences, or a closely related, quantitative field.

ABOUT GRYPS

Gryps is an AI operating system for the architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) industry. Institutional owners such as hospital systems, universities, and airport authorities run multi-billion-dollar capital programs on data scattered across emails, spreadsheets, network drives, and disconnected systems of record. Gryps connects that information and gives owner teams an AI operating system for their capital programs, so they can find answers, manage risk, automate their work and make decisions faster.

We are a product-focused organization that dreams big and achieves those dreams. Our customers are large players in the construction industry. This is an opportunity to be part of a nimble team where every individual is an expert in their area. We work fast, iterate quickly, and create a product that transforms how our customers work through AI.

This is the place for you if you’ve worked in a role at the intersection of AI, automation, data analytics, construction tech, construction management, and innovative technology-and you’re looking for the next leap in your career. You will have direct influence over the growth of Gryps within customer organizations, our product roadmap, and impact on the Gryps bottom line.

We’re a growing company backed by Primary Ventures, LDV Capital, Pear VC, and other top investors. You will work directly with the CEO and our customers-large organizations that own and operate hospitals, universities, and public infrastructure.

THE ROLE

We're hiring a Head of AI Deployment to lead a team of 4-6 in turning Gryps deployments into measurable value for our customers. You'll own the full post-sale relationship: understanding each customer's program, designing the data strategy behind their deployment, identifying the use cases that matter most, guiding the implementation team to fast, repeatable time to value, and measuring the success of the deployment.

This is a player-coach role. You'll work directly with owner executives and program leaders while developing early-career professionals into strong implementers and advisors. You'll also be accountable for renewals and expansion, because customers who get real value are the ones who grow with us.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

LEAD AND DEVELOP THE TEAM

- Manage, coach, and grow a team of 4-6 customer success and implementation professionals, many early in their careers. Set clear expectations, give direct feedback, and build their construction domain knowledge and client-facing confidence.

- Build the playbooks, standards, and rituals that make delivery consistent: onboarding frameworks, implementation checklists, account reviews, and health scoring.

DEFINE VALUE AND DATA STRATEGY

- Work with customers to find the highest-value use cases across their capital programs, such as cost and change tracking, schedule risk, document and contract intelligence, closeout, and portfolio reporting. Prioritize them by business impact and feasibility.

- Design the data strategy for each use case: which sources to connect, how unstructured and structured data is organized and validated, and how outputs tie back to the customer's systems of record and decisions.

- Turn customer outcomes into clear, quantified value stories that executives and champions can carry into their own organizations.

OWN CUSTOMER RELATIONSHIPS

- Serve as trusted advisor and executive sponsor for your accounts, from project and program managers up to VPs of Facilities, Capital Planning, and Real Estate.

- Lead executive business reviews that connect product usage to program outcomes and set the agenda for what comes next.

- Represent the customer's voice internally, partnering with Product and Engineering on requirements, feedback, and roadmap priorities.

DRIVE PRODUCT ENGAGEMENT AND IMPLEMENTATION EFFICIENCY

- Own adoption and engagement metrics across your book of business. Spot drifting accounts early and step in before they become risks.

- Run implementation for speed

title: Customer Success Engineer (Internship)
description:
Join BLP and help make the world’s business processes autonomous!
Our agentic platform helps finance and operations teams worldwide remove manual work from their core business processes, so work runs end-to-end with greater control and significant productivity gains.
Today, over 550 enterprise customers use BLP across 1,300+ deployed projects. In the processes we automate, customers achieve productivity improvements of 5 to 10 times.
To date, BLP remains majority employee-owned, with Goldman Sachs holding a minority stake as a growth investor. Our success is driven by deep expertise in technology and business processes, a superior product with strong product-market fit, reflected in an expanding customer base that includes Fortune 500 companies.
BLP is one of Switzerland's fastest-growing SaaS scale-ups; we are now entering our next phase of growth. From our headquarters on Zürich's Bahnhofstrasse, we're expanding globally, with a growing presence across Europe and North America.
Join us and help make autonomous operations the new standard.
Location
This is a six-month internship based at our HQ in central Zurich or in Munich. This is an in-person role. You learn this job by sitting next to people who already do it, and that does not work remotely.
About the role
Think of this role as the modern Sherlock Holmes - new puzzles to solve and new people to work with, every single day.
This role sits exactly at the intersection of technology and business, and that is not a figure of speech. On one side you are in the system, in the data, working out what actually happened. On the other you are on a call with a finance team explaining it and agreeing what to do. You need both, every day.
Our customers run their finance and supply chain processes on blp. When something does not behave the way they expected, a document that did not post, an exception that should have resolved itself, a number in a dashboard that looks wrong, they write to us. That is where your work starts, and it is also where you become the face of blp for that customer. What reaches them is you: your answer, your explanation, your judgement about what to do next.
You will not be reading from a script and escalating. You investigate what the system did, what the data says and what the customer's process actually requires. You have the access and the authority to change configuration when that is the answer. And when it is not, you know who to bring in and what to give them.
The role grows with you. You start on cases where the pattern is known and someone is close by. As your expertise builds you take the harder ones, and your exposure to customers grows with it: from written answers, to calls, to being in the room when a customer wants their most pressing problem solved now.
This goes well beyond tickets. We are a fast-moving organisation and a lot of what needs to exist does not exist yet. You will take on and drive initiatives that make the whole operation scale: a recurring problem that should be solved once rather than fifty times, a piece of tooling that does not exist, a way of working that has outgrown itself. Interns here have shipped things that the team still uses.
How we think about ownership
You will be given real work with real consequences, early, because that is the only way anyone learns this job properly. The other half of that is judgement: explore and decide for yourself where you can, and pull someone in when something critical is on the line. Knowing which situation you are in is part of the skill, and nobody will hold it against you for asking. What matters is that you are the face of blp to that customer, and that you take that seriously.
Most of our customers work in German and you will be in front of them from early on. That is uncomfortable for about three weeks and then it is the best part of the job.
This is a real internship, not an observation post. You will be trusted with live customers quickly, with people close by while you learn.

Scholar Rock is delivering muscle-targeted breakthroughs to transform the treatment of spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) and other rare neuromuscular diseases where muscle atrophy remains a critical unmet need.
As a global leader in myostatin biology, a field focused on proteins that regulate muscle mass, the biopharmaceutical company is named for the visual resemblance of a scholar rock to protein structures. Our commitment to unlock fundamentally different treatment approaches is powered by broad application of a proprietary platform, which has developed novel monoclonal antibodies to modulate protein growth factors with extraordinary selectivity. Scholar Rock works every day to create new possibilities for patients through its highly innovative anti-myostatin program, including opportunities in additional rare neuromuscular diseases. Learn more about our neuromuscular franchise at ScholarRock.com and follow @ScholarRock on X and on LinkedIn.
 
Summary of Position:

Scholar Rock is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

title: Executive Operations Coordinator
description:
World Animal Protection are looking for an Executive Operations Coordinator to help us move the world to protect animals.

As an Executive Operations Coordinator, you'll be the trusted operational partner to a member of our Global Leadership Team. You will be able to smooth complexity out of their day and give them the space to focus on strategy rather than logistics. It's a role built on judgement, trust, and quiet initiative. You will be empowered with real scope to shape how things get done.

What you'll do

• Coordinate plans, projects and delivery with stakeholders internally and externally.

• Own complex diaries, inboxes and cross-timezone scheduling, keeping everyone briefed and on time.

• Organise travel and accommodation for board members, executives and guest speakers, in line with policy.

• Structure timelines and sequence activity so leaders can execute complex pieces of work with confidence.

• Track delivery of time-bound priorities e.g. org planning, reviews, key initiatives.

• Keep oversight of actions, milestones and dependencies, following through with clarity and diplomacy.

• Provide support at global meetings, capturing outcomes and next steps in real time.

• Identify priorities, risks and upcoming demands before they become problems.

• Act as a strategic filter for competing priorities.

• Contribute to shared global event logistics, including trustee travel and visas.

• Collaborate with fellow Executive Operations Coordinators to close gaps and keep coverage seamless.

What can we offer you?

We are offering a competitive salary and benefits including.

• Help saving for your retirement - join our pension scheme and we’ll match contributions up to 6%

• 24 days’ holiday per year when you join, plus an additional day with each year of service up to 5 days

• Opportunity to flex public holidays to an alternate day that better suits an employee and their beliefs.

• Additional 3 days to be taken at the end of the calendar year.

• 2 global Wellbeing midyear closure days

• Flexibility - the opportunity to choose start times that align with both business needs and your work-life balance, ensuring the right fit for both the job holder and the role requirements

• Life Assurance - all World Animal Protection employees receive Life Assurance. Under the Death in Service benefit scheme the employee will receive 3x annual salary to go to their nominated beneficiary.

• Volunteer Leave - 2 days per year to volunteer for a cause of your choice

• A range of 'Inclusivity Benefits': providing various types of leave to support belonging and inclusion at work and to assist our employees during critical moments. This includes leave for Bereavement, Carers, Disability, Menstrual/Menopause, Pregnancy Loss, Fertility Treatment, Gender Affirming Medical needs, Companion Animal Bereavement, and 'Pawternity' leave.

• Long Service Milestones to celebrate 10 year anniversary (and every subsequent 5 years) with bonus day off and employee 'shout out'

• 24/7 Employee Assistance Programme and Employee Wellbeing Portal

Our commitment to equity, diversity and inclusion

To achieve our aim of making World Animal Protection a Diverse and Inclusive employer, we particularly welcome applications from individuals of traditionally under-represented communities and backgrounds.

Our values and behaviours

At World Animal Protection we recruit with our values & behaviours in mind. Please bear this in mind through your application journey. These are:

•
Global: We make decisions & act with a global mindset

•
Diverse and Inclusive: We actively encourage and promote diversity, ensure all voices are heard and included and are committed to equal opportunities for all

•
Collaborative: We work together and co-create to achieve lasting change

•
Agile: We make change happen in a fast-moving world

•
Growing People: We continually learn and develop

OptiMindHealth (OMH) is expanding and seeking compassionate psychotherapists to join our team and work remotely from the comfort of their home. Today, OMH provides superior behavioral health services patients in Massachusetts and Colorado. Since 2016, we’ve specialized in serving both adult and adolescent patients in a supportive outpatient environment. Individual psychotherapy is the most common clinical work performed, but our clinicians also perform family therapy, group therapy, and psychological testing as needed and/or appropriate to a wide range of presenting problems of our patients.

title: Technical Program Manager

description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

About the Team

Core Technology is the engineering backbone of Anduril's hardware platforms - the shared systems, components, and infrastructure that power products across every division. The team develops and sustains the critical electromechanical systems, drive systems, propulsion, actuation, and embedded electronics that make Anduril's autonomous systems work. 

About the Role

We're looking for a Technical Program Manager to own the planning, execution, and delivery of hardware development programs within Core Tech. You'll be the connective tissue between design engineering, manufacturing, supply chain, test, and operations - driving complex electromechanical products from concept through production. You'll work directly with engineering leads to build roadmaps, track milestones, manage risks, and make sure the right teams are engaged at the right time. If you've driven hardware programs and want to do it at startup speed on systems that matter, this is the role.

What You’‘ll Do

• Represent and help build your program’s culture. As the liaison to the engineering development organization you are well positioned to consistently interact with all teams at Anduril and often will be tasked to represent the program in a cross-functional capacity. You should be knowledgeable of not only the current state of the program, but also the various technical and operational factors which define the product architecture and overall vision.

• Establishing key milestones and targets from across the organization to help define the product roadmap. This will require an in-depth understanding of what teams are affected by the various stages of your program’s engineering development. You are to ensure that teams are being engaged at the right time and at the right maturity stage to be successful. The roadmap you help develop would be the guide for your program that the organizations would reference and plan around.

• Evaluate and prioritize the various tasks required to successfully support the program development efforts. Be prepared to help drive to the best decision for the program and company. This generally should be a data driven approach, and should include inputs from all the various stakeholders to ensure the decision is well informed and can be successfully executed.

• Execute a variety of tasks to ensure the program stays on track. These tasks can take many forms as the engineering program manager should be prepared to fill any gap to de-risk the roadmap.

• Communicate engineering strategy and vision to the technical stakeholders to help manage expectations. Ensure all risks are noted and addressed with adequate time and resources to help keep things on track.

• Expected to work closely with teams including, but not limited to: design engineering, finance, logistics, EHS, manufacturing, supply chain, engineering testing, legal, technical operations, business strategy/programs, and production

title: Licensed Mental Health Counselor (LMHC) - Holyoke, MA
description:
Licensed Mental Health Counselor (LMHC) $70 K-85K/yr

Position Requirement: Remote Full-Time and Part-time Positions Available

If you are looking for a new opportunity to grow with a clinician founded and clinician led organization, look no further! As an authentic, unique, and skilled counselor, you have a plethora of options when it comes to work. Hospitals, community clinics, investment bank funded group practice startups, state agencies, and more.

At OptiMindHealth , we continuously strive to provide consistent, high-quality care and expand the reach of mental health care services in our communities. Unfortunately, the need often outpaces the services available to those we serve and only adds to the current mental health crisis in our nation. To combat this crisis and further our mission, we need more compassionate and skilled clinicians to join our cause. We are not interested in the “burnt-out” clinician that no longer finds meaning in their work and is just going through the motions; we are seeking people with a passion to provide excellent care, and the belief that we, together, can make a difference. If that’s you, then you’re in the right place!

Our approach with our team is simple, we take care of you, the clinician, so you can take care of patients. How do we do that? By investing in your growth, supporting you financially, holistically, and professionally, while being flexible regarding your personal needs and goals. The work we do with patients is hard enough and over the years we have found that our team often does their best work when the administrative burdens are taken off their plate and they are able to be fully present with their patients. Our administrative support team handles all non-clinical tasks so that you don’t have to think about anything except focusing on your patients.

Why bother with the endless administrative burdens and isolation of private practice? Use your highly trained interpersonal skills to change the culture around mental health care, decrease stigma, and help people who need you, while being supported by an experienced multi-disciplinary team of clinicians. Let us take care of the rest!

Want to work part time? No problem. Want to do group therapy? Sure! Want to do long-term psychodynamic psychotherapy with all of your clients? We do it every day. Interested in treating couples? We can make that happen. Basically, what we are saying is that whatever outpatient care you are interested in providing, we can surely accommodate you. We know you have exceptional skills; we want you to be part of our team.

The perfect candidate will share our passion for improving and expanding access to high quality mental health care and will thrive in a culture that emphasizes creativity, authenticity, humor, compassion, acceptance, and determination. Telehealth or onsite, we support your authentic and unique growth trajectory, while being yourself and having some fun!

We prioritize the clinician's experience by offering excellent compensation, benefits, training/supervision, and flexibility. Whether you’re working from home or in one of our physical offices, if you’re doing it during your scheduled work hours, you’re getting paid for it. Our compensation packages include:

• Starting Salary range: $70,000.00 - $85,000.00 per year.

• 401K with maximum employee matching.

• Health care benefits.

• Generous paid vacation and sick leave time.

• Paid administrative time for consultation, supervision, and documentation.

• Full administrative support.

Here are a few extra perks our team loves:

• Paid supervision, clinical rounds, and administrative time.

• Customized schedules within available clinic hours.

• Hybrid work environment if desired: Telehealth and/or in-person (in select locations).

The CRO oversees credit, operational, market, liquidity, compliance, fraud, cyber, conduct, and reputational risks while ensuring alignment with the bank's strategic objectives, regulatory requirements, and risk appetite.

Enterprise Risk Management

title: Marketing Project Manager
description:
About TurFresh

TurFresh is a growing artificial turf cleaning and maintenance company serving residential and commercial
customers across multiple U.S. markets. Our marketing team includes specialists in content, creative, paid media, SEO, local search, CRM, and automation.

We are hiring a Marketing Project Manager to connect those specialties and ensure approved marketing work is planned, completed, published, tracked, and reported accurately.
The Opportunity

Our marketing strategy and specialist capabilities are in place. The opportunity is to make execution more
consistent, visible, and accountable.

This role owns the delivery process that moves marketing initiatives from approved direction through verified completion. You will manage campaign and project schedules, coordinate contributors, resolve routine delivery issues, perform assigned publishing and quality assurance work, and maintain an accurate record of progress and results.

This is not a role for someone who only schedules meetings, sends reminders, or updates task lists. We need someone who takes ownership, recognizes incomplete work, resolves problems independently, and makes sure campaigns and projects reach the finish line correctly.

You will not replace our specialists or independently set marketing strategy. Specialists remain accountable for the quality, accuracy, and documentation of their craft. You will own the delivery system: handoffs, schedules, dependencies, readiness, assigned publishing, completion evidence, and reporting preparation.

What You Will Own

Campaign and Project Delivery

• Turn approved campaign or project direction into an actionable delivery plan with owners, deadlines, dependencies, approval points, and success measures.

• Manage campaigns and marketing projects from handoff through verified publication or completion and initial performance reporting.

• Identify missing assets, overdue reviews, conflicting priorities, and delivery risks before they affect launch dates or business outcomes.

• Resolve routine execution issues directly and escalate material risks with a concise explanation and recommended next step.

• Maintain clear visibility into what is complete, what remains open, what is blocked, and who owns the next action.

Production and Publishing

• Coordinate copy, design, video, landing pages, email, social content, tracking, and other campaign components without absorbing the specialists' craft responsibilities.

• Perform assigned routine publishing work across approved email, social media, website, CRM, and content platforms.

• Schedule approved content and campaigns accurately and on time.

• Make routine website or landing page updates using established templates.

• Confirm that the correct copy, creative, links, tracking, audiences, and approvals are in place before publication.

• Verify successful publication and document completion evidence.

Quality Assurance and Campaign Readiness

• Use established checklists and the approved brief to review customer-facing materials before launch.

• Confirm required business, creative, technical, legal, and tracking approvals.

• Return incomplete submissions for correction rather than moving them forward.

• Verify links, forms, phone numbers, tracking parameters, formatting, mobile presentation, audiences, and calls to action.

• Document errors, rework, and recurring breakdowns so the underlying process can be improved.

Marketing Operations

• Maintain the marketing calendar, production queue, campaign checklists, approval records, and recurring work schedule.

• Keep project management systems accurate and current so leadership does not need to reconstruct project status.

• Organize campaign assets, final versions, supporting documents, and completion evidence.

• Document repeatable workflows and maintain marketing standard operating procedures.

• Track vendor and specialist commitments, deadlines, dependencies, and unresolved items.

Trainline is Europe's leading independent rail platform, helping millions of travellers find and book the best value rail and coach journeys across our app, website and partner channels. Our Financial Control team sits at the heart of how we understand and run the business, owning the quality and integrity of our management accounts, balance sheet and month end processes. title: Product Manager, Growth
description:
ABOUT FACTORY

Our mission is to create a world where software builds and improves itself.

We build the platform for self-improving software development, helping the world's largest enterprise engineering teams turn their organizations into autonomous software factories. Customers including Nvidia, Blackstone, Royal Bank of Canada (RBC), Palo Alto Networks, Adobe, and T-Mobile run Factory to ship code, review PRs, run tests, and deploy continuously - getting smarter with every cycle.

In 2026, we raised $200M at a $5B valuation, bringing our total funding to over $400M. We are backed by world-class investors and operators including Khosla Ventures, Sequoia, Blackstone, Ali Ghodsi (CEO of Databricks), and Frank Slootman (Former CEO of Snowflake).

ABOUT THE ROLE

As the PM for Growth at Factory, you’ll own our overall approach to get users active and productive on the platform.

You’ll be responsible for our activation metric: how do we measure what it means to be an activated user, and how do we get more users to that point and beyond, whether they’re coming from our self-serve product or onboarding via an enterprise deployment.

And you’ll own our self-serve product offering: what we provide as part of it, how we price and package it, the role it plays in our broader company strategy, and how we should evaluate its success.

There won’t be a single “growth” engineering team to work with-you’ll operate across multiple engineering pods and work closely with our Marketing, BizOps, and Deployment functions to make sure we’re doing the right things to create more happy Factory users.

You’ll need a strong thesis for what makes a compelling early software factory experience in a competitive market, and an opinion about how PLG best reinforces a top-down Enterprise motion. You’ll need sharp technical instincts, genuine empathy for developers, and the ability to make fast, high-quality decisions in ambiguity. You should be as comfortable diving into technical architecture discussions as you are presenting roadmap priorities to leadership.

Our goal with the product function at Factory is to be high-leverage, high-ownership, and hands-on-you can expect to be working directly with the C-suite at the largest companies in the world, and shipping improvements directly to the product. And you’ll be central to defining the role of Product in a software factory-driven organization-a pattern we intend to pioneer and then help distribute across our customer base and the broader industry.

Why this role exists
The architecture set in this role decides which certifications One Identity can hold and which markets we can sell into. That is unusual commercial weight for an engineering seat, and it comes with a mandate from leadership to build the program behind it.
We sell on-premises and hosted solutions. Some products run as hosted services we operate in Azure and AWS. Others ship as software customers deploy in their own datacenters. Infrastructure security here has two audiences: the environments we run, and the base images, container definitions, and deployment defaults we publish, which become part of every customer's environment. A hardening decision made once is inherited by everyone who deploys it.
We're separating from Quest Software and building an independent security function. The team is lean and globally distributed, and this role is its senior technical voice. Scope comes from what you design and automate, and from what engineering chooses to adopt.
What you'll do
Shape the architecture

• Own security architecture across Azure and AWS: tenant, subscription and account design, network segmentation and traffic control, private connectivity, egress policy, workload isolation. Where a regulated market or a certification constrains a design, you're expected to know before it's committed.

• Run our own products against real security requirements and tell us what you find. IT operates our privileged access controls on One Identity software, so you'll see how our products hold up under production pressure and take that back to the teams building them.

• Bring engineering into architectural decisions early. Designs teams help shape are the ones that hold up in production.

Raise the engineering bar

• Teams already build with infrastructure as code across both clouds. Raise the security ceiling inside that practice: hardened modules, secure-by-default landing zones and account baselines, and patterns teams reach for because they're better.

• Extend policy as code across the pipeline and the platform so teams get a signal at commit time.

• Own the hardened image pipeline for virtual machines and containers, covering the fleet we run and the images we publish: build, patch cadence, provenance, signing, and the automation that keeps both current.

• Secure the container orchestration layer, including the reference architecture and secure defaults customers inherit when they deploy our products on their own clusters.

• Set the security architecture for AI workloads: model and inference endpoint exposure, data boundaries and residency, identity for agents and service principals, secrets handling, and guardrails around AI tooling in the development lifecycle.

Reduce exposure and prove it

• Own infrastructure vulnerability and exposure management end to end: discovery, prioritization weighing exploitability and reachability alongside severity, ownership routing, remediation tracking, verification. Hosted services and customer-deployed software have different release paths and the practice accounts for both.

• Elevate cloud posture and workload protection into a single practice spanning Azure and AWS. You set the platform direction, the coverage standard both clouds are held to, and the path findings take to the teams that own them.

• Drive the decisions on where agentic workflows belong in security engineering: where automation acts and where it recommends, how its output gets verified, and what has to hold true before teams trust it. Where a person still has to act, the finding arrives with owner, fix path, and rationale. Where we can act ourselves, it arrives as a pull request against the module, image definition, or policy that produced it. PRs, not tickets.

title: Import Compliance Manager
description:
JOB SUMMARY:
The Import Compliance Manager is responsible for ensuring the company's import operations comply with U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) regulations and all applicable trade laws. This role oversees the accurate classification of imported goods under the Harmonized Tariff Schedule (HTS), manages relationships with customs brokers and freight forwarders, and coordinates the end-to-end flow of container shipments from origin to destination, including bonded warehouse operations and duty drawback recovery. The ideal candidate combines deep trade compliance expertise with hands-on experience managing container logistics and import documentation.
JOB DUTIES:

• Manage the classification of imported products under the Harmonized Tariff Schedule (HTS), ensuring accuracy and consistency across the product catalog.

• Oversee end-to-end container import operations, including booking, customs clearance, port coordination, and delivery to distribution centers or warehouses.

• Serve as the primary point of contact for customs brokers, freight forwarders, and carriers to resolve clearance delays, documentation discrepancies, and duty disputes.

• Ensure compliance with CBP regulations, Importer Security Filing (ISF) requirements, and other federal import/export regulations.

• Maintain and audit import records, entry summaries, and classification rulings to support recordkeeping requirements and prepare for CBP audits.

• Manage bonded warehouse operations, including inventory control, CBP-mandated recordkeeping, withdrawal entries, and coordination with warehouse operators to ensure compliance with 19 CFR Part 19.

• Monitor changes in tariff schedules, trade agreements, and duty rates (including Section 301, antidumping/countervailing duties) and assess their impact on the business.

• Identify and pursue duty savings opportunities, including free trade agreement eligibility, bonded warehouse deferral strategies, duty drawback, and first sale valuation.

• Administer the company's duty drawback program end-to-end: identify eligible import/export transactions, prepare and file drawback claims, maintain supporting documentation, and manage relationships with drawback service providers or brokers to maximize duty recovery.

• Partner with procurement, finance, and legal teams to evaluate landed cost impacts of tariff changes and sourcing decisions.

• Develop and maintain internal compliance policies, standard operating procedures, and training materials for classification and import processes.

• Manage and mentor import compliance analysts or coordinators, as applicable.

• Track key performance metrics related to container transit times, customs clearance rates, and compliance audit outcomes.

REQUIREMENTS:

• Bachelor's degree in International Business, Supply Chain Management, Logistics, or related field.

• 5+ years of experience in import compliance, customs brokerage, or international trade, with direct experience in HTS classification. Strong working knowledge of CBP regulations, Incoterms, and international shipping documentation (bills of lading, commercial invoices, certificates of origin).

• Experience managing container shipments and coordinating with ocean carriers, freight forwarders, and customs brokers.

• Experience with bonded warehouse (Class 3) operations and duty drawback claim preparation and filing.

• Familiarity with trade compliance software and ERP/TMS systems (e.g., SAP GTS, Oracle GTM, Descartes).

• Licensed Customs Broker (LCB) credential preferred, not required.

• Excellent analytical, organizational, and cross-functional communication skills.

• Ability to manage multiple shipments and deadlines in a fast-paced environment.

$90,000 to $120,000, DOE

About the Team:

The User Management team owns the full identity lifecycle at AlphaSense - from creating and provisioning users, through managing their identities, to authenticating who they are and authorizing what they can do in the system. Our work spans three core domains:

• User Management - creating, provisioning, and managing user identities

• Authentication - verifying who users are

• Authorization - determining what users can do in the system

We are a product platform team, not a product team: we build the identity and access infrastructure that other engineering teams build on top of, rather than shipping user-facing features ourselves. We also act as a security guardrail for AlphaSense, since identity and access sit at the center of how the platform stays secure.

The team is well-established and senior, based in Helsinki, Finland. We're now expanding into North America - with roles based in both Canada and the US - to build follow-the-sun coverage, so our customers get proper support around the clock, and to push deliberately toward a true platform model - scaling our authentication and authorization systems so they can be safely self-served by teams across the company.

About the Role: 

This is a Staff Engineer role on the team that manages identity and access for AlphaSense's entire, and constantly growing, customer base, and that nearly every product engineering team depends on for user and entitlement data. You'll work across all three pillars of identity: creating and managing users, authenticating them, and authorizing what they can do - designing systems built to scale with a constantly growing number of users. Security is core to this role, not adjacent to it - you'll work closely with our security teams to make sure what we build is secure by design, in an environment governed by SOC2 and GDPR.

We're looking for a genuinely senior, self-sufficient engineer with strong experience building and operating identity, authentication, or authorization platforms at scale, ideally in a platform/product-platform engineering context. This is someone who doesn't just execute a roadmap, but helps understand the needs behind it, shapes it, and then drives execution - largely autonomously, and in close collaboration with our core team based in Helsinki. Verian Lithuania (formerly PPMI ) is a European policy research and evaluation consultancy. We work primarily for EU institutions (European Commission, JRC, DG SANTE, HaDEA, EUDA, ECDC) and international organisations (OECD, UN). Our public health and life sciences portfolio is growing fast, and we are looking for an experienced Healthcare Project Manager to help us deliver it.
THE ROLE
We are looking for a project manager to lead large-scale, complex EU-funded healthcare projects: multi-year, often multi-partner contracts with several parallel workstreams, high-profile EU clients and demanding delivery standards. You will be accountable for delivery from kick-off to final reporting, including budgets, timelines, teams and client relationships.
Our portfolio includes European guidelines for prostate cancer, evidence-based research prioritisation in the drugs field, GRADE evidence assessments, and quality indicator development following Cochrane standards. You will work closely with our review methodologists, so a good understanding of how systematic reviews and guidelines are developed will help you plan, steer and quality-assure this work as we grow our in-house evidence synthesis capacity.
Day-to-day, you would:

• Lead projects end to end: work planning, timelines, budgets, risk management and quality assurance of deliverables

• Manage several projects and workstreams in parallel, setting priorities and allocating resources across teams

• Act as the main point of contact for EU clients, including inception, interim and final reporting in line with contractual requirements

• Lead multidisciplinary teams of researchers, review methodologists, external experts and consortium partners

• Organise and steer working groups, expert panels and stakeholder consultations

• Oversee the planning and quality of systematic reviews, GRADE assessments, guideline development and quality indicator work, in close collaboration with methodologists

• Drive the use of innovative and AI-assisted review tools in project workflows

• Lead or contribute to tenders and proposals for EU evidence synthesis and health contracts

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR
Essential:

• PhD in public health, epidemiology, health sciences or a related field

• Proven track record of managing large-scale, complex projects (e.g., multi-year, multi-partner contracts with several parallel workstreams), ideally EU-funded healthcare or public health projects such as service or framework contracts with the European Commission and its agencies, EU4Health or Horizon Europe

• Experience holding full responsibility for project budgets, timelines, risk management and contractual reporting

• Experience leading multidisciplinary teams and managing senior client and stakeholder relationships

• Excellent written and spoken English

Strong assets:

• Understanding of how systematic reviews and clinical guidelines are developed (e.g., Cochrane methodology, PRISMA, GRADE, Evidence-to-Decision frameworks)

• Hands-on systematic review experience as an author or review team member

• Experience in cancer evidence review, such as screening, diagnosis, treatment guidelines or HTA

• Track record of writing or leading successful EU tender proposals

• Experience with AI/ML tools in evidence synthesis or health data analysis (e.g., AI-assisted screening, text mining, bibliometrics)

• Publications in cancer, screening, HTA or guideline development

• Familiarity with review and analysis tools (e.g., RevMan, GRADEpro, Covidence, R, Python)

• Experience drafting policy or regulatory documents

CONDITIONS

• Monthly service fee: EUR 4,000-4,500, depending on experience

• Full-time equivalent commitment with flexible working hours

• Remote work within the EU

• Service contract with possibility of extension

HOW TO APPLY
Please submit your CV and a short cover letter by 6 November 2026, highlighting your experience managing EU-funded healthcare projects and any relevant work in cancer

title: Operations Lead - Process Change
description:
About Reserv

Reserv is an insurtech creating and incubating cutting-edge AI and automation technology to bring efficiency and simplicity to claims. Founded by insurtech veterans with deep experience in SaaS and digital claims, Reserv is venture-backed by Bain Capital and Altai Ventures and began operations in May 2022. We are focused on automating highly manual tasks to tackle long-standing problems in claims and set a new standard for TPAs, insurance technology providers, and adjusters alike. We have ambitious (but attainable!) goals and need people who can work in an evolving environment. If building a leading TPA and the prospect of tackling the long-standing challenges of the claims role sounds exciting, we can't wait to meet you.

Location Requirement

Candidates must reside in an eligible U.S. state throughout employment. We are unable to hire candidates residing in California, Alaska, Hawaii, U.S. territories, or outside the United States.

About the Role

Reports to the Operations Principal, Change. The Strategic Operations team sits between Product, Technology, and Claims Operations and owns the work that turns a new way of working into one the organization actually runs on.

Not every change at Reserv arrives with a product release behind it. Programs change, client requirements change, and the way a claim is handled changes with them. We are hiring an Operations Lead to own process design and change across claims operations, so that how work is done is written down, current, and changed deliberately.

You own the process side of the function: before-and-after process design for each change, the SOP library and how it is governed, verification that changes landed in practice, and the training and communications for process changes. You will work alongside the Operations Lead who owns product change, since most product releases also change a process, and with claims leadership, who own the work you are documenting. You will be an excellent fit if you have redesigned how an operations team works, can write a process someone will follow, and verify that changes landed in practice.

Duties & Responsibilities

Process Design: Lead the before-and-after process design for each change, product-driven or not, working with leaders, managers, and team leads on what actually shifts in their day. Write the end-to-end process so it can be followed without further explanation, and pressure-test it with the people who will run it before it goes live.

SOP Ownership and Governance: Own the SOP library across lines of business and account variants: its structure, its currency, and its governance. Draft the standard language for each change, drive it into every affected SOP through the SOP owners against a date, and build the auditability that shows who changed what and when. Partner with the Principal on the platform and workflow the library should run on.

Change Readiness for Process Changes: Run process changes against the readiness standard: documented process, approved change plan, training and communications plan, onboarding updated, and metrics defined. Assemble the evidence for sign-off and flag gaps early.

Training, Enablement, and Communications: Build and execute the training and communications for process changes for leaders, managers, and frontline teams, and coordinate with Learning & Development so new-hire onboarding teaches the current process.

Verification and Feedback: Go back after each change and verify it landed in practice, through SOP checks, time studies, and conversations with the teams doing the work. Carry what you find back to the Principal and to claims leadership, and feed it into how the next change is designed.

Metric and Data Management: This person will be responsible for continually tracking metrics to determine success and make data-driven changes to rollouts

description:
WHY BACKEND ENGINEERING AT LANGFUSE

Your work will have an outsized impact.

Langfuse ingests terabytes of AI tracing data per day. When a Fortune 50 company instruments their application with Langfuse, they hit the infrastructure you built. Everything you ship is open source and immediately visible.

The core of your role is making Langfuse fast and affordable at scale: owning the ingestion pipeline, optimizing ClickHouse data models and queries so dashboards load instantly, and building the backend abstractions that let product engineers ship data-heavy features without reinventing the plumbing each time.

You will also make sure Langfuse runs everywhere. You’ll operate Langfuse Cloud across multiple production environments, and make self-hosting effortless. You will support a single Docker Compose setup to enterprise-grade Helm chart deployment.

 

You won’t be solving these problems alone. Langfuse is now part of ClickHouse, which means the people who built the database you’re optimizing are one channel away. Few backend roles give you that kind of access to the internals of your core datastore.

 

YOU WILL GROW AT LANGFUSE BY

- Own and optimize our ingestion pipeline: Langfuse ingests massive volumes of tracing data through a pipeline that flows from our API to ClickHouse. You'll work on throughput, latency, reliability, and cost efficiency at every stage of this pipeline.

- Make ClickHouse fast: our tracing data lives in ClickHouse. You'll design schemas, optimize merge strategies, tune batch inserts, write and review analytical queries that power dashboards and the UI. You'll become an expert on ClickHouse internals - and you'll have the ClickHouse database engineering team one channel away.

- Build new infrastructure-heavy features: things like LLM-as-a-Judge (where we post-process large volumes of ingested data asynchronously), alerting at scale, client-code execution, or batch dataset operations. Build the foundation and, if you like, dip your toes into the frontend for those.

- Test with real data in production: when evaluating a new ClickHouse schema, migration, or query optimization, you'll run load tests against production data to validate that changes actually improve things. We don't guess at performance. We prototype new table designs, run them in parallel on real traffic, and compare before committing.

- Scale for what's next: we're growing fast and new product directions like complex long-running agent observability and real-time evaluation push the infrastructure in new ways. You'll be thinking ahead about what breaks at 10x scale.

 

LEARN MORE ABOUT OUR INFRASTRUCTURE

title: Ingeniero de Plataforma
description:
2Brains es una consultora tecnológica que impulsa el crecimiento y la evolución de organizaciones líderes en Latinoamérica. Diseñamos y construimos el futuro digital de nuestros clientes a través de una integración profunda y estratégica de negocio, experiencia y tecnología , convirtiendo desafíos complejos en impacto real.
Hoy, 2Brains forma parte de Acid Labs , uno de los principales grupos de consultoría tech e innovación de la región. Esta adquisición fortalece nuestra propuesta de valor, ampliando nuestra escala, capacidades tecnológicas y presencia regional, y nos permite acompañar a nuestros clientes con soluciones más robustas, ágiles y de alto impacto en todo su ciclo de transformación.
Contamos con un equipo multidisciplinario de más de 250 especialistas en estrategia, diseño, tecnología, datos e inteligencia artificial. Combinamos visión estratégica con ejecución de excelencia para crear plataformas tecnológicas, productos digitales y experiencias omnicanal que escalan, generan eficiencia y mejoran la relación entre las organizaciones y sus usuarios.
En 2Brains no solo asesoramos: diseñamos, prototipamos, implementamos y escalamos . Trabajamos como socios estratégicos de nuestros clientes, ayudándolos a acelerar la toma de decisiones, reducir riesgos y capturar valor tangible a través de la innovación digital.

El ingeniero/a de la plataforma 2Brains debe

Diseñar y mantener infraestructuras seguras y escalables que impulsen la velocidad y la eficiencia de los equipos de desarrollo . Se apoya en prácticas de infraestructura como código (Terraform, Ansible) para automatizar el aprovisionamiento y asegurar entornos consistentes y reproducibles
Además, incorpora observabilidad y monitoreo para optimizar el desempeño y costos, y gestionar la plataforma como un producto , con foco en el Developer Experience (DevEx) . También lidera iniciativas de AI-Enhanced Operations , habilitando la detección temprana de anomalías, auto-remediación y escalamiento predictivo.
¿Qué desafíos tendrá el/la Ingeniero/a de Plataforma?

•
Evolución de CI/CD: Diseñar, mantener y mejorar pipelines de integración y desplegar continuo, asegurando lanzamientos rápidos, seguros y confiables.

•
Colaboración y consultoría interna: Trabajar conjuntamente con los equipos de desarrollo, entendiendo sus flujos de trabajo y transformando sus necesidades en soluciones de infraestructura efectiva.

•
Soporte operativo y resolución de bloqueos: Atender incidencias y brindar apoyo técnico en el día a día del ciclo de desarrollo, garantizando que los equipos puedan entregar valor sin fricciones.

•
Definición de estándares y documentación: Crear y mantener lineamientos claros que mejoren la calidad del proceso de implementación y fomenten la autonomía de los desarrolladores.

•
Automatización: Detectar tareas repetitivas o complejas dentro del ciclo de vida del software y desarrollar scripts o herramientas que simplifiquen y automaticen estos procesos.

¿Qué conocimientos buscamos en el/la Ingeniero/a de Plataforma?

•
Experiencia en CI/CD: Manejo sólido de herramientas como GitLab CI (ideal), Jenkins o GitHub Actions .

•
Experiencia en Cloud Computing: Preferentemente en Google Cloud Platform (GCP) .

•
Kubernetes (nivel usuario): Capacidad para implementar aplicaciones, gestionar manifiestos y realizar problemas de servicios (no se requiere experiencia avanzada en administración del clúster).

•
Programación y scripting: Conocimientos prácticos en Python o Bash para automatización y desarrollo de herramientas internas.

•
Infraestructura como Código: Experiencia con Terraform será considerada una ventaja.

•
Deseable: Conocimientos en autoescalado con KEDA , Service Mesh (Istio) o Cloud Functions en GCP .

•
Orientación al servicio y empatía: Habilidad para comunicarse de forma efectiva con equipos de desarrollo, comprender sus desafíos y priorizar soluciones que mejoren su experiencia diaria.

title: Customer Success Manager Public Sector (m/w/d)
description:
Wir bei SoSafe haben das Ziel, der führende Anbieter für Human Risk Management Lösungen in Europa zu werden. Unsere preisgekrönte Awareness-Plattform unterstützt Unternehmen dabei, nachhaltige Verhaltensänderungen durch effektive, interaktive Trainings rund um Cyber-Sicherheit und Datenschutz zu erzielen. Prognosen zufolge wird Cyberkriminalität die Welt bis 2025 jährlich 10,5 Billionen Dollar kosten - werde Teil der Lösung und gestalte die Zukunft der Cybersicherheit aktiv mit!

So trägst du dazu bei:

Mit deiner kunden- und produktorientierten Denkweise betreust du deine Kunden und sorgst für deren Erfolg mit der SoSafe-Produktsuite. Du bist verantwortlich für den Aufbau von Beziehungen und kommunizierst deinen Kunden den Mehrwert des Einsatzes der SoSafe Produkte, um die Kundenbindung zu steigern und auszubauen.

Zu deinen Aufgaben in unserem Customer Success Team gehören:

- Aufbau langfristiger Kundenbeziehungen durch lösungsorientierte Beratung

- Beratung von Kunden in Bezug auf Maßnahmen zur Sensibilisierung für Cybersicherheit

- Proaktive Unterstützung der Kunden bei der Erreichung ihrer Ziele

- Konzeption und Durchführung von Business-Reviews

- Verwaltung von Kampagnen zur Förderung des Sicherheitsbewusstseins bei den Kunden von SoSafe und Aufzeigen des ROI

- Einbringen von Feedback in unser Produktentwicklungsteam als Stimme des Kunden

- Nutzung der Kundenbeziehung, um aus Kunden Fans zu machen

Was dich auszeichnet:

- Du bist kundenorientiert und möchtest deine Kunden unterstützen, ihre Ziele zu erreichen

- 2+ Jahre praktische Erfahrung als Customer Success Manager oder in einer anderen kundenorientierten und beratenden Funktion (Vertrieb, Beratung, etc.)

- Exzellente Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift (weitere Sprachkenntnisse sind erwünscht)

- Du sicher in der Identifikation und Verhandlung kommerzieller Details mit Kunden (Vertragsverlängerungen und Upsells)

- Du bist in der Lage, mehrere interne und externe Stakeholder bei einer Vielzahl von Kunden und Projekten zu managen

- Du hast Erfahrung in einer SaaS-Umgebung und bist bereit, dich weiter in die sich entwickelnde Technologie einzuarbeiten

- Du bist ein Teamplayer und möchtest Teil eines dynamischen Teams sein, das stetig voneinander lernt

- Du hast Verständnis dafür, wie technische Initiativen in geschäftlichen Nutzen umgesetzt werden

Was wir bieten*:

- Work-Life-Balance: Flexible Arbeitszeiten, 33 Tage Urlaub

- Well-being und finanzielle Unterstützung: Zugang zur Open-Up App, Mitarbeiterrabatte

- Verbindung & Gemeinschaft: Virtuelle Events, gemeinsame Teamaktivitäten und Möglichkeiten für lokale Treffen

- Und vieles mehr: Technische Ausstattung, Empfehlungsprämien, hundefreundliches Büro

*Die oben genannten Vergünstigungen gelten für Vollzeitmitarbeiter und können je nach Standort leicht variieren. Dies ist nur eine Auswahl - mehr erfährst Du im Verlauf des Bewerbungsprozesses.

Über uns

Wir bei SoSafe haben es uns zur Aufgabe gemacht, die digitale Welt sicherer zu gestalten, indem wir den menschlichen Faktor in der Cybersicherheit in den Mittelpunkt stellen.

Als eines der am schnellsten wachsenden Security-Awareness-Scale-ups weltweit nutzen wir verhaltenswissenschaftliche Erkenntnisse und datengesteuertes Lernen, um Menschen effektiv gegen Cyber-Bedrohungen zu stärken. Unser Human Risk Management-Ansatz unterstützt Unternehmen dabei, ihre Mitarbeiter*innen zum wirkungsvollsten Schutzschild gegen Sicherheitsrisiken zu entwickeln.

Mit der Unterstützung führender VCs wie Highland Europe und Global Founders Capital expandieren wir weltweit in rasantem Tempo. Wir suchen Teamplayer, die sinnvolle Veränderungen im Bereich Cybersicherheit vorantreiben, Verantwortung übernehmen und gemeinsam mit uns wachsen wollen.

Wenn du in einem lebendigen, zielorientierten Umfeld aufblühst, das Innovation, Vielfalt und Zusammenarbeit großschreibt - dann bist du bei uns genau richtig!

title: Senior Data Engineer
description:
GenLogs is a transportation-technology company building the next generation of truck intelligence. Through a nationwide network of sensors and proprietary data, we deliver real-time, high-fidelity insights into freight movement for commercial supply-chain customers and public-sector agencies. Our mission is to strengthen America’s logistics backbone, combat freight fraud and cargo theft, and provide near-instantaneous visibility into commercial motor vehicle activity across major freight corridors. By operating at the intersection of edge sensing, computer vision, AI-driven analytics, and large-scale field deployment, GenLogs is transforming how transportation data is captured, secured, and commercialized.
ABOUT THE DATA TEAM
The Data Science team at GenLogs transforms raw observational data from the Trident sensor network into high-value intelligence used by law-enforcement agencies, regulators, ports, and private-sector freight operators. We build models, analytics, and measurement frameworks that enable vehicle detection, entity resolution, behavioral insights, fraud and theft indicators, compliance signals, and network-wide operational performance metrics. Our work sits at the center of the freight intelligence platform, shaping how billions of roadside observations become actionable information. We partner closely with Engineering and Product to deploy algorithms at scale and with Go-to-Market teams to define customer-facing analyses that drive real operational outcomes. The team blends statistical rigor, ML capability, and domain expertise to create a new standard for freight intelligence in the United States.
ABOUT THE JOB
You’re a problem solver at heart. You thrive at the intersection of engineering, computer science, and data, you’re motivated by questions that don’t have obvious answers, and you love to architect and build reliable systems that enable whole organizations to build world class analytics. You bring a background in engineering, computer science, physics, applied math, or another hard science discipline, and you enjoy applying that technical foundation to real-world data challenges.
You are energized by ambiguity, obsessed with understanding how complex systems behave, and capable of breaking down big problems into tractable iterations. You ask great questions, validate assumptions with data, and are relentless in your pursuit of signal over noise.
WHAT YOU’LL DO

• Build and maintain ETL/ELT pipelines using Python and SQL.

• Develop ingestion workflows with AWS Firehose , S3, and related services.

• Create and optimize dbt models, tests, and incremental logic.

• Tune Snowflake queries and warehouse usage for cost and performance.

• Operate and improve Airflow DAGs for reliable execution and monitoring.

• Maintain high data quality, data integrity, and pipeline SLA commitments.

• Bring clarity to ambiguous requirements and propose practical solutions.

• Lead data engineering best practices and influence architectural decisions.

• Drive projects independently, from definition to delivery.

• Collaborate with engineering, analytics, and ML teams to support shared goals.

• Build feature pipelines to support ML workflows.

• Support model deployment, monitoring, and automated retraining.

• Add data validation and quality checks across ML and analytics pipelines.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

•
5+ years of experience in data engineering or software engineering.

• Strong Python and SQL skills.

• Hands-on experience with Snowflake , AWS Firehose/S3 , Airflow , and dbt .

• Ability to work independently and execute in a dynamic environment.

• Strong problem-solving skills and attention to detail.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Experience with geospatial data (e.g., spatial joins, geometry processing, or geospatial libraries).

• Experience with ML or MLOps pipelines.

• Knowledge of Snowflake streams, tasks, and performance tuning.

• Experience with large-scale or semi-structured datasets.
